skill.name: security-guardian
skill.description: Provides structured application-security guidance for code reviews, secure design, and remediation across OWASP risks, authentication, authorization, secrets, and cryptography.
skill.summary: Review application security risks and plan practical remediations.
skill.author: Bikach

security_audit.summary: All 400 static matches are false positives in context. The repository is a Markdown-only defensive application-security reference library, and the matched strings are examples, checklists, or descriptions of threats and controls. No executable code, credential access, network activity, or prompt-injection attempt was found in the reviewed material.

remediation.issue: Static scanners interpret instructional attack examples as active behavior.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly labeled as non-executing defensive material and consider scanner exclusions for Markdown reference content.

remediation.issue: The skill documentation names common shell tools for security reviews.
remediation.suggestion: State that any command must be reviewed and approved by the user before execution, especially when scanning repositories or handling secrets.

content.value_statement: Security reviews can miss common weaknesses across authentication, input handling, and sensitive data. This skill provides organized defensive guidance and practical review checklists for secure implementation decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guides reviews for common web risks, including injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, XXE, and path traversal.
Explains secure patterns for passwords, MFA, JWTs, sessions, OAuth, RBAC, and IDOR prevention.
Provides checklists for cryptography, secrets handling, API security, data protection, and security logging.
Helps translate identified weaknesses into defensive remediation steps and validation questions.
Supports review of sensitive changes using the included security domains and OWASP-oriented checklists.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not execute a penetration test or verify a running system.
It cannot prove that an implementation is secure without access to relevant code and configuration.
It does not replace organization-specific threat modeling, legal review, or incident response procedures.
Recommendations require human validation against the application architecture and deployment environment.

use_cases.title: Review a pull request
use_cases.description: Identify security questions and remediation priorities for a change affecting user input, authorization, or data handling.

use_cases.title: Design a secure feature
use_cases.description: Use the relevant guidance before implementing login, file upload, API, or payment-related functionality.

use_cases.title: Create a security review checklist
use_cases.description: Build a repeatable checklist for releases and audits using the OWASP, secrets, logging, and cryptography references.

prompt_templates.title: Check a login feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this login feature for password storage, MFA, session, and JWT security issues. Provide prioritized defensive recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Review file uploads
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file upload flow for path traversal, content validation, storage, and permission risks. List concrete safeguards to implement.

prompt_templates.title: Assess an API change
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this API change for authentication, authorization, CORS, rate limiting, input validation, and error-handling risks. Produce a review checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a focused remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the supplied code and architecture, create a remediation plan for the identified OWASP risks. Include priority, ownership, validation steps, and residual risk.

output_examples.input: Review an endpoint that accepts a user-controlled filename.
output: Risk: path traversal through untrusted filenames
Safeguards: generate server-side names, constrain storage paths, validate file type and size
Validation: add tests for traversal attempts and unauthorized file access

output_examples.input: Review a new OAuth callback flow.
output: Require state and PKCE where applicable
Do not accept arbitrary next URLs
Log failures without recording tokens or personal data

best_practices: Provide the relevant code, configuration, data flow, and trust boundaries for an accurate review.
Prioritize findings by exploitability, impact, and exposure before scheduling remediation.
Validate every recommendation with tests, code review, and deployment-specific controls.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a checklist as proof that a production system is secure.
Do not paste real credentials, private keys, tokens, or personal data into a review request.
Do not apply generic remediation without confirming framework behavior and application context.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers defensive application-security topics, including OWASP risks, authentication, authorization, secrets, cryptography, APIs, and logging.

faq.question: Can it perform a penetration test?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and remediation planning, not automated exploitation or verification of a live system.

faq.question: Which code changes are good candidates?
faq.answer: Authentication, authorization, file uploads, APIs, user input, data storage, and integrations that handle sensitive information are good candidates.

faq.question: Does it support OWASP reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include OWASP-oriented checklists and guidance for common web application weaknesses.

faq.question: Should I provide secrets for review?
faq.answer: No. Replace credentials, tokens, keys, and personal data with safe placeholders before sharing material.

faq.question: Does it guarantee compliance?
faq.answer: No. Compliance requirements depend on your organization, jurisdiction, system scope, and evidence collection process.
